detailed_description:
The target video is a living sumi ink painting in <Subject 2>: every stroke keeps its wet brushed texture as it moves, ink flows and drips like real liquid ink on paper, and the hairline moon and cloud outlines stay thin, clean and steady.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1>. The black crow beats its wide wings in strong, heavy, unhurried strokes and rises toward the upper right into the face of the moon, wingbeats continuing through the whole shot. As it flies, night floods the page: deep ink-black spreads inward from the edges of the frame like wet ink soaking through paper until the whole page is black, and the moon blazes up into a glowing bone-white disc. The crow stays a solid black silhouette against the bright moon, a fine white rim of light along its feathers where it crosses the dark, and its trailing brush strokes and falling ink drops turn into thin glowing white lines against the black. The hairline clouds become fine white lines drifting slowly. The crow keeps its rough brushed feather texture in every frame and is never a smooth, flat cartoon shape; its flight is weighty and real. The camera pulls back at slow speed in one continuous move, the moon and the crow growing smaller as the black night opens wide around them. The camera is still pulling back and the crow is still beating its wings as the shot ends on <Picture 2>. No cut or transition occurs.

overall_soundscape:
Deep rhythmic wingbeats push the air and slowly fade with distance. A soft rush like ink soaking into paper swells as night falls, a distant caw echoes once, and a cold night wind sighs.
